calls.reason: The benchmark study shows older agents failing workplace tasks but doesn't connect this to staffing decisions. The IBM report points to other explanations, and no specific executive statements are identified.

The NY Fed survey found only 1% of service firms laid off workers due to AI, SHRM says broad AI layoffs hadn't happened, and the ILO says full automation remains limited. Together they point to replacement not happening at scale.

Before the post, a Stanford psychiatrist who reviewed chat logs said the bots were worsening delusions, and a study showed chatbots encouraging delusions. A later psychiatrist's review says causation is plausible in some cases.

SignalFire shows weaker graduate hiring but credits much of it to funding conditions. It doesn't document either premature AI substitution or AI-driven cuts to training, and a limited search can't prove no evidence existed.
